Phylogeny
¨Tracing Phylogeny
¤Protein Comparisons
  nImmunological techniques
    nDegree of cross reaction used to judge relationship
  nAmino acid sequencing
    nSimilar sequence in the same protein indicates a close relationship
¤Molecular Clock
  nUse neutral (non-adaptive) nucleotide sequences
  nAssumes a constant rate of mutation over time
explanation: Protein comparisons and molecular clocks are advanced methods for tracing phylogeny. Protein comparisons include immunological techniques, where the degree of antibody-antigen cross-reaction is measured to estimate species relationships, and direct amino acid sequencing, where highly similar sequences in the same protein indicate a close evolutionary relationship. The Molecular Clock is a method that uses neutral, non-adaptive nucleotide sequences. By assuming that these neutral mutations accumulate at a relatively constant rate over time, scientists can estimate the absolute time that has elapsed since two species diverged from a common ancestor.

questions.q: What is a molecular clock used for in systematics?
opts: To determine the rate of soil erosion in an ecosystem
To estimate the absolute time of evolutionary divergence based on a constant rate of neutral mutations
To measure the physical size of organisms over time
To cause hybrid sterility in plants
questions.exp: A molecular clock uses neutral nucleotide sequences and assumes a constant mutation rate over time to estimate when species diverged from their common ancestor.

questions.q: How can protein comparisons indicate evolutionary relationships?
opts: By measuring the size of cells
Through immunological cross-reaction degrees and similarities in amino acid sequencing
By calculating the number of Hox genes
By assessing whether a protein can become a fossil
questions.exp: Protein comparisons evaluate relationships by measuring the degree of cross-reaction in immunological tests or by comparing the alignment of amino acid sequences in shared proteins.
